title: Sell with confidence, handle objections and keep a sales book

say: Sell with confidence, handle objections, and keep a sales book.
This is the video for Module 3 of Introduction to Pricing and Selling.
A good price only becomes money when someone buys. Selling is a short, friendly conversation in five stages.
First, greet warmly. Use her name, put the phone down, and on WhatsApp reply quickly.
Second, ask before you tell. Who is it for? When does she need it? What matters most to her?
Third, show benefits. A feature is a fact. A benefit is what that fact does for her. Link them with the words, which means.
Fried fresh on the morning of delivery, which means it is crunchy when your guests eat it.
Fourth, state the price plainly, with one benefit next to it. Do not apologise, and do not say you can reduce.
Fifth, ask for the sale. How many packs would you like? Shall I deliver on Thursday or Friday?
Most lost sales skip stage 2 or stage 5.

panel.heading: Five stages of a sale
panel.rule: Say the price with a benefit, then stop talking.

say: Here is how it sounds. Ngozi greets Funmi and asks who it is for. Funmi says it is a birthday party of about 25 children on Saturday.

card.title: A WhatsApp order for a party

say: Ngozi suggests 200 g packs, one sealed pack per child, fried fresh on Friday. The price is 800 naira a pack, so 20,000 naira for 25 packs, delivered on Saturday morning.

say: Then she asks for the sale, with a 50% deposit of 10,000 naira to confirm.
Funmi pays. Ngozi checks her bank app, sees the money, and sends a written confirmation.

say: An objection is a reason a customer gives for not buying yet. It is normal, and it shows she is still interested.
First, listen to the whole objection without defending yourself.

panel.heading: Four steps for any objection
items: Ask a question to find the real worry

say: Second, acknowledge it. I understand, you want to be sure it is worth the money.

panel.heading: Four steps for any objection
items: Ask a question to find the real worry

say: Third, ask. Is it the total amount, or are you comparing with another seller?

panel.heading: Four steps for any objection
items: Ask a question to find the real worry

say: Fourth, respond with value, a smaller size, or honest facts. Notice that none of these starts with a price cut.

say: In many markets buyers expect to bargain, so plan before you start.
Amaka decides an asking price of 18,000 naira, a target of 17,000 naira, and a walk-away price of 15,000 naira, which is above her cost.
The customer offers 12,000 naira. Amaka asks when she needs it, and explains she can deliver in time for the wedding, with a free adjustment.
She agrees at 17,000 naira, paid in full today. Her profit is 6,000 naira.
Sell honestly. Describe your product truthfully, give the full quantity you advertise, and be honest about delivery time.

panel.heading: Honest selling builds repeat sales
left: Give the full weight you advertise
Promise only what you can do
right: Claim it cures or lasts forever
Meet in the middle every time

say: Do not make claims you cannot prove. Do not meet in the middle each time, or you will end far below your plan. Move in small steps, and only for something in return, like full payment.
If a buyer only wants a price below your cost, wish her well.

say: Records turn guesses into facts. Write each sale: date, item, quantity, price, sales amount, cost, profit and how she paid.
On Monday, Ngozi sold 12 packs at 800 naira, 30 bulk packs at 750 naira, and 8 small packs at 450 naira.
Her sales were 35,700 naira and her profit was 11,100 naira. That is a margin of 31%, just as she planned.
Check your cash and your app against the book the same day.
Each week, write five numbers: total sales, gross profit, margin, discounts given, and your best and slowest items.
Sales can rise while profit falls. A falling margin is your early warning to recalculate costs.
To remember. Follow the five stages and ask for the sale. Answer objections calmly before you ever cut a price. Plan your three prices. Write every sale.
And to see if a fixed cost like rent is worth it, divide it by your profit per item.

panel.heading: Remember
items: Greet, ask, show benefits, state price, ask for the sale
Plan asking, target and walk-away prices
Write every sale and check your margin weekly
Break-even = fixed costs divided by profit per item

say: Now write your own five-stage script and practise your price sentence out loud ten times. Prepare answers to your three most common objections, and keep your sales book for 7 days.
